idiom_name: framework-supplied separation: view/page function as supply half, template or render helper as presentational half
implementation_notes: Python's split comes from the web or data-app framework rather than from the language. In server-rendered stacks the view function is the supply half - it loads objects and hands a context to a template - and the template (or a partial rendered with explicit context) is the presentational half; keep templates to formatting what they were given, because a Django or Jinja template can call methods on whatever the context exposes, which is how a presentational template silently becomes a data-access layer. In data apps the same split is a page function plus stateless render helpers: Streamlit keeps per-session values in st.session_state across reruns, so a helper that takes plain values and calls the owner's callback is a pure function of the state it is handed. What replaces the classic container component is the framework's own request or rerun boundary; a hand-written model object plus render functions is only needed for desktop or CLI loops where no framework supplies it - or when Qt/PySide is used, in which case Qt's model/view classes apply.
code_sketch:
def render_lines(lines, on_remove):            # presentational half: values in, event out
    for line in lines:
        if st.button(f"remove {line['sku']}", key=f"rm-{line['sku']}"):
            on_remove(line["sku"])

def cart_page():                               # supply half: owns the data source
    st.session_state.setdefault("lines", load_lines())
    render_lines(st.session_state.lines, on_remove=remove_line)
pitfalls: A template that calls side-effecting methods on context objects is doing data access inside the presentational half; pass plain values or read-only view models instead.
Session state is tied to the connection: a browser reload or a link navigation resets it, so it is not durable storage for anything the view needs later.
Module-level caches or globals used to 'share' data between requests leak one user's data into another user's render.
A render helper that reads the data store directly stops being renderable in isolation; pass it the values it prints.
